subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: 'Behold, I have given you every plant yielding seed which is upon the face of all the earth, and every tree with seed in its fruit...' In the statement above, God made provision for man to
explanation: Genesis 1:29 continues: 'you shall have them for food.' God provided plants and fruit trees as food for man.
proTip: Genesis 1:29: plants and fruit are given 'for food'.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: God told Noah that 'Whoever sheds the blood of man, by man shall his blood be shed...' because
options: man is made in God's image
blood is the life of man
explanation: Genesis 9:6 gives the reason: 'for God made man in his own image.' Human life is sacred because of the divine image.
proTip: Reason for the ban on murder in Genesis 9:6: man is in God's image.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
question: What did God promise the Israelites after their rescue from Babylon to make them fear Him for ever?
options: A new heart and a new life
A new covenant and a new spirit
explanation: Jeremiah 32:39 (RSV): 'I will give them one heart and one way, that they may fear me for ever, for their own good and the good of their children after them.' The promise follows the return from exile (32:37).
proTip: Jeremiah 32:39: 'one heart and one way' to fear God for ever.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: The LORD appeared to Abraham and promised his descendants the land of the Canaanites at
explanation: Genesis 12:6-7: Abram passed through the land to the oak of Moreh at Shechem; 'Then the LORD appeared to Abram and said, "To your descendants I will give this land."'
proTip: Genesis 12:7: the first promise of the land came at the oak of Moreh, at Shechem.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: When Joseph narrated his second dream, he was rebuked by Jacob because the dream would
options: make his brothers all the more jealous
subject his parents to his authority
send the family to Egypt as slaves
explanation: In the second dream the sun, moon and eleven stars bowed to Joseph. Jacob rebuked him: 'Shall I and your mother and your brothers indeed come to bow down to the ground before you?' (Genesis 37:10).
proTip: The second dream had his parents bowing down to him.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Deborah was a judge when Israel was under the yoke of
explanation: Judges 4:2-3: the LORD sold Israel into the hand of Jabin king of Canaan, whose commander was Sisera. Deborah judged Israel during this oppression.
proTip: Deborah and Barak vs Jabin and Sisera of Canaan.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: Divine Providence, Guidance and Protection - Jacob at Bethel (Genesis 28:10-19)
question: When Jacob woke from sleep on his way to Haran, he was afraid and named the place Bethel because he believed that the
options: place was a part of heaven
place had a ladder that led to heaven
angels of the Lord lived there
place was the gate of heaven
explanation: Genesis 28:17: 'How awesome is this place! This is none other than the house of God, and this is the gate of heaven.' He named it Bethel, 'house of God'.
proTip: Bethel = house of God; gate of heaven.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: God rejected the sons of Eli from being priests over His people because they were
explanation: 1 Samuel 3:13: 'his sons were blaspheming God, and he did not restrain them.' Hophni and Phinehas also despised the offering of the LORD (2:12-17).
proTip: Eli's sons blasphemed and Eli did not restrain them.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: The final consequence of Saul's disobedience to God was his
explanation: After repeated disobedience (1 Samuel 13; 15; 28), Saul was wounded in the battle on Mount Gilboa and died (1 Samuel 31:1-6).
proTip: Saul's disobedience ended with his death on Gilboa.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: God forgave David when he took Bathsheba, the wife of Uriah, because
options: the child he had with her died
David fasted and lay upon the ground
David was a man after God's heart
explanation: David said, 'I have sinned against the LORD,' and Nathan replied, 'The LORD also has put away your sin' (2 Samuel 12:13). Confession came first.
proTip: Forgiveness followed David's confession.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Abner sent messengers to David at Hebron because he wanted to
options: bring over all Israel to David
spy on Hebron and capture it later
explanation: 2 Samuel 3:12: Abner sent messengers saying, 'Make your covenant with me, and behold, my hand shall be with you to bring over all Israel to you.'
proTip: Abner offered to bring all Israel over to David.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: Decision Making - Solomon at Gibeon (1 Kings 3:4-5)
question: Where did the LORD appear to Solomon in a dream?
explanation: 1 Kings 3:4-5: Solomon offered sacrifices at the great high place at Gibeon, where 'the LORD appeared to Solomon in a dream by night.'
proTip: Solomon's request for wisdom came at Gibeon.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
question: The division of David's kingdom was a direct consequence of
explanation: Rehoboam rejected the elders' advice and threatened heavier burdens (1 Kings 12:13-14), so the northern tribes rebelled. Solomon's forced labour was the background, but Rehoboam's decision was the direct cause.
proTip: Rehoboam's rejection of the elders' advice split the kingdom.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
subTopic: Greed and its effects - Gehazi (2 Kings 5:20-27)
question: Naaman's leprosy was transferred to Gehazi as a result of
options: the testimony of the maid of Israel
the gifts he received from Naaman
the bath Gehazi took in the river Jordan
explanation: Gehazi took gifts from Naaman deceitfully, and Elisha said, 'the leprosy of Naaman shall cleave to you' (2 Kings 5:27). Greed was the cause.
proTip: Gehazi's greed brought him Naaman's leprosy.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
subTopic: The Supremacy of God - Elijah on Mount Carmel (1 Kings 18:36-38)
question: The prayer of Elijah in the name of the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob brought down fire from heaven which
options: killed all the prophets of Baal
destroyed the demonic spirits of Jezebel
explanation: 1 Kings 18:38: 'Then the fire of the LORD fell and consumed the burnt offering, and the wood, and the stones, and the dust.'
proTip: The fire consumed the offering, proving the LORD is God.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
subTopic: Religious reforms in Judah - Josiah (2 Kings 22:8-13; 23:1-3)
question: The reforms of King Josiah were made possible by the
options: discovery of the Book of the Law
destruction of the chariots of Ahaz
explanation: Hilkiah found the Book of the Law in the Temple (2 Kings 22:8); when it was read, Josiah tore his clothes and began reforms (22:11; 23:1-3).
proTip: Josiah's reform started with the discovery of the Book of the Law.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
question: As Nehemiah embarked on reconstruction of Jerusalem, he faced threats and opposition from
explanation: Nehemiah 2:10; 4:1-8; 6:1-14 name Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite as the main opponents, with Geshem the Arab.
proTip: Nehemiah's opponents: Sanballat, Tobiah and Geshem.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
subTopic: Social justice and true religion - Amos 6:12
question: Amos told the Israelites that they had turned justice into
explanation: Amos 6:12: 'you have turned justice into poison and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood.' (Amos 5:7 says 'turn justice to wormwood', so check against your key.)
proTip: Amos 6:12: justice turned into poison; righteousness into wormwood.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
question: Hosea compared Judah's love for the LORD to the morning cloud because it
options: goes away early like the dew
goes up to God like smoke
explanation: Hosea 6:4: 'Your love is like a morning cloud, like the dew that goes early away.' It was fleeting and insincere.
proTip: Hosea 6:4: love like morning cloud and dew - quickly gone.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
question: The attribute of God which Isaiah emphasizes most is His
explanation: In Isaiah 6:3 the seraphim cry 'Holy, holy, holy'; Isaiah repeatedly calls God 'the Holy One of Israel' (e.g. 1:4).
proTip: Isaiah's key title for God: the Holy One of Israel.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
subTopic: Social justice and true religion - Isaiah 1:15
question: '...even though you make many prayers, I will not listen...' Why will God, the Holy One of Israel, not listen?
options: Because they sacrifice with incense to Him
Because God detests their burnt offerings of rams
Because their hands are full of blood
Because their new moon gifts are a burden to Him
explanation: Isaiah 1:15 gives the reason: 'your hands are full of blood.' Worship does not please God when it is joined with injustice and violence.
proTip: God rejects worship from hands full of blood.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
question: How did God convince Jeremiah of his divine call?
options: He spoke to him directly from heaven
He sent a prophet to inform him
explanation: Jeremiah 1:9: 'Then the LORD put forth his hand and touched my mouth; and the LORD said to me, "Behold, I have put my words in your mouth."'
proTip: The touch on Jeremiah's mouth = divine authority to speak.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
question: The vision of the dry bones of Ezekiel portrays
explanation: Ezekiel 37:11-14: the bones are the whole house of Israel; God promises to open their graves and bring them back to their land. The vision is one of hope.
proTip: Dry bones = hope of national restoration.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: What was Peter's reaction when he saw the great shoal of fish he and his partners caught?
explanation: Luke 5:8: Simon Peter fell down at Jesus' knees, saying, 'Depart from me, for I am a sinful man, O Lord.'
proTip: Peter's response to Jesus' power: 'I am a sinful man'.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: In the feeding of the five thousand, according to Matthew, the first thing that Jesus did was to
options: order the loaves and fish to be brought to Him
break the loaves and fish brought to Him
look up to heaven and pray to God
give thanks to God and have the fish and loaves shared
explanation: Matthew 14:19: 'he took the five loaves and the two fish, and looking up to heaven, he blessed, and broke and gave the loaves to the disciples.' Looking up and blessing came before breaking and giving. (Verse 18, 'Bring them here to me', comes earlier, so check against your key.)
proTip: Order at the meal: take, look up and bless, break, give.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: According to John, the six stone jars of water which Jesus turned into wine were kept there for the
explanation: John 2:6: 'Now six stone jars were standing there, for the Jewish rites of purification.'
proTip: The jars were for Jewish purification rites.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: When the man with an unclean spirit in the region of the Gerasenes saw Jesus, he
options: acknowledged Him as the Son of the Most High God
pleaded to be cast into the Abyss
requested to follow Him as a disciple
pleaded that a miracle be performed to cleanse him
explanation: Mark 5:6-7: he ran and worshipped Jesus and cried, 'What have you to do with me, Jesus, Son of the Most High God?' (The abyss plea, Luke 8:31, was by the demons and about being sent into the abyss; the request to follow Jesus came after healing.)
proTip: Even the unclean spirit recognised Jesus as the Son of the Most High God.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: 'To you it has been given to know the secrets of the kingdom of heaven, but to them it has not been given...' This statement was made after Jesus had told the parable of the
explanation: After the parable of the sower, the disciples asked why He spoke in parables, and He answered with this statement (Matthew 13:3-11).
proTip: Why parables? Jesus answers after the sower.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: The parable of the lost sheep portrays the shepherd as being
explanation: The shepherd leaves the ninety-nine and searches until he finds the lost sheep, then rejoices (Luke 15:4-6), showing God's love for sinners.
proTip: The shepherd stands for God's seeking love.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: '...Do not lay up for yourselves treasures on earth...' This statement shows that Jesus
options: does not want Christians to be rich
wants Christians to seek first the kingdom of God
regards poverty as a condition for the kingdom of God
explanation: The passage continues, 'seek first his kingdom and his righteousness, and all these things shall be yours as well' (Matthew 6:33). The point is priorities, not poverty.
proTip: Treasure in heaven: put God's kingdom first.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: Jesus commissioned the twelve disciples charging them to
options: go to all the world and preach
go to the lost sheep of the house of Israel
receive hospitality and wages for their labour
perform healing miracles among the Samaritans
explanation: Matthew 10:5-6: 'Go nowhere among the Gentiles, and enter no town of the Samaritans, but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.'
proTip: The first mission of the twelve was to Israel alone.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Triumphal Entry and Temple Cleansing - Mark 11:11
question: According to Mark, after Jesus had triumphantly entered Jerusalem, He
options: went to Bethany with the twelve
wept over the city and prophesied its destruction
addressed the Pharisees who had asked Him to rebuke His disciples
explanation: Mark 11:11: 'he entered Jerusalem, and went into the temple; and when he had looked round at everything, as it was already late, he went out to Bethany with the twelve.' Weeping over the city and the Pharisees' request are in Luke 19.
proTip: In Mark, Jesus goes into the temple, looks round, then leaves for Bethany.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Trials and Death of Jesus - Matthew 27:37
question: According to Matthew, the inscription over Jesus when He was crucified was
options: 'This is the King of the Jews'
'Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews'
'This is Jesus the King of the Jews'
explanation: Matthew 27:37: 'And over his head they put the charge against him, which read, "This is Jesus the King of the Jews."' Mark has 'The King of the Jews'; John has 'Jesus of Nazareth, the King of the Jews'.
proTip: Each gospel words the inscription differently - match the gospel.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: Which disciple asked Jesus, 'Lord, we do not know where you are going; how can we know the way?'
explanation: John 14:5 records Thomas's question, to which Jesus replied, 'I am the way, and the truth, and the life.'
proTip: John 14:5: Thomas asks; Jesus says 'I am the way'.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Fellowship in the Early Church - Acts 1:15-20
question: '...for he was numbered among us, and was allotted his share in this ministry...' What happened to Judas, the person referred to in the statement above?
explanation: Acts 1:16-20 speaks of Judas, who acquired a field with the reward of his wickedness and 'falling headlong he burst open'; Matthew 27:3-5 says he hanged himself. The death of Judas is traditionally taught as suicide.
proTip: Judas' death opened the way for Matthias to be chosen.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Fellowship in the Early Church - Acts 6:1-6
question: The disciples in the early church chose the seven deacons in order to
options: solve the problem of murmuring by the Hellenists
have adequate daily distribution of food
take proper care of the neglected widows
devote themselves to prayer and teaching the word
explanation: Acts 6:1: 'the Hellenists murmured against the Hebrews because their widows were neglected in the daily distribution.' The seven were chosen to settle this, freeing the apostles for prayer and the word (6:2-4). Options B-D are parts of the same account, but A states the immediate problem.
proTip: Acts 6: the murmuring of the Hellenists led to the choosing of the seven.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: The sound which came from heaven on the day of Pentecost is likened to that of
explanation: Acts 2:2: 'a sound came from heaven like the rush of a mighty wind, and it filled all the house.'
proTip: Pentecost: sound like a mighty wind, then tongues like fire.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Mission to the Gentiles - the Jerusalem Council (Acts 15:1-5)
question: What were the major issues of controversy that led to the appearance of Paul and Barnabas before the Council in Jerusalem?
options: Circumcision and food offered to idols
Unchastity and the Law of Moses
Circumcision and the Law of Moses
The Law of Moses and pollution by idols
explanation: Acts 15:1, 5: some taught that unless Gentiles were circumcised 'according to the custom of Moses' they could not be saved, and said they must keep the law of Moses.
proTip: The Council debated whether Gentile converts must be circumcised and keep the law of Moses.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: According to John, the distinctive quality of the disciples of Jesus Christ is
options: laying down their lives for others
explanation: John 13:35: 'By this all men will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.'
proTip: The mark of a disciple: love for one another.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: God has extended the promise He made to Abraham to all those who share his faith based on
explanation: Romans 4:13: 'the promise... did not come through the law but through the righteousness of faith.' Verse 16 says it is 'by faith, in order that the promise may rest on grace' and be guaranteed to all his descendants, those who share his faith.
proTip: Abraham's promise came through the righteousness of faith, not the law.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: According to Galatians, what makes all believers sons of God is
explanation: Galatians 3:26: 'for in Christ Jesus you are all sons of God, through faith.'
proTip: Sonship through faith in Christ Jesus.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: Speaking in tongues, according to Paul, is allowed where
options: there is one with the gift of interpretation
the Holy Spirit is present during worship
those speaking in tongues are many
explanation: 1 Corinthians 14:27-28: 'If any speak in a tongue, let there be only two or at most three... and let one interpret. But if there is no one to interpret, let each of them keep silence in church.'
proTip: Tongues need interpretation in public worship.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
subTopic: Christian living in the community - Romans 12:8
question: Paul says that anyone who does acts of mercy should do so with
explanation: Romans 12:8: 'he who does acts of mercy, with cheerfulness.' Liberality is for giving and zeal for leadership.
proTip: Romans 12:8: mercy with cheerfulness.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: Paul advises Christians to obey authorities because
options: rulers want people to obey them
explanation: Romans 13:1: 'there is no authority except from God, and those that exist have been instituted by God.'
proTip: Authorities have divine mandate, so obey them.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: The second coming of Christ shall be recognized by
options: earthquakes and wars, darkness on earth
explanation: 1 Thessalonians 4:16: 'the Lord himself will descend from heaven with a cry of command, with the archangel's call, and with the sound of the trumpet of God.'
proTip: Signs of the Parousia in Paul: cry of command, archangel's call and trumpet.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: 'And the dead in Christ will rise first; then we who are alive, who are left, shall be caught up together with them in the clouds to meet the Lord in the air.' From the statement above, Paul's belief was that he would
options: live to witness the second coming of Christ
have died before the second coming of Christ
resurrect at the second coming of Christ
have been in paradise before the second coming
explanation: Paul writes 'we who are alive, who are left', including himself among those who may still be alive at the Lord's coming (1 Thessalonians 4:15, 17).
proTip: Paul expected the Lord to return in his lifetime.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: According to James, whoever keeps the whole law but fails in one point
options: has become guilty of all of it
will be punished for a little while
explanation: James 2:10: 'whoever keeps the whole law but fails in one point has become guilty of all of it.'
proTip: Breaking one commandment makes one a lawbreaker.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
subTopic: Christian living in the community - James 1:2-4
question: James, in his Epistle, urged the brethren to count their trials as joy because the testing of their faith produces
explanation: James 1:3: 'the testing of your faith produces steadfastness.'
proTip: Trials produce steadfastness (endurance).

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
subTopic: Christian living in the community - 1 Peter 4:16
question: According to Peter, if a Christian suffers for his faith, he should not be
explanation: 1 Peter 4:16: 'yet if one suffers as a Christian, let him not be ashamed, but under that name let him glorify God.'
proTip: Do not be ashamed of suffering as a Christian.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: Peter says that Christians would put to silence the ignorance of foolish men by
explanation: 1 Peter 2:15: 'it is God's will that by doing right you should put to silence the ignorance of foolish men.'
proTip: Doing right silences critics.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Joseph called the name of his first-born Manasseh, meaning God has
options: made him forget his hardship and his father's house
made him fruitful in the land of his affliction
rescued him from the hands of Potiphar
made him not to forget his brothers and his household
explanation: Genesis 41:51: 'God has made me forget all my hardship and all my father's house.' Ephraim means 'God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction' (41:52).
proTip: Manasseh = forgetting; Ephraim = fruitfulness.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: '...Now therefore lighten the hard service of your father and his heavy yoke upon us, and we will serve you.' This request was made to Rehoboam because
options: the people had another person in mind
the people wanted to test his wisdom
explanation: 1 Kings 12:4: 'Your father made our yoke heavy. Now therefore lighten the hard service of your father... and we will serve you.' The people wanted relief from forced labour and heavy taxes.
proTip: The northern tribes asked for relief from Solomon's burdens.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: 'You are the man...' This statement by Nathan made David immediately
options: order him out of the palace
order the killing of the child
explanation: 2 Samuel 12:13: David said to Nathan, 'I have sinned against the LORD.' Nathan replied that the LORD had put away his sin.
proTip: Nathan's parable led David to confess immediately.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: One of the consequences of Saul's disobedience was that
explanation: In the battle on Gilboa, Saul was wounded by Philistine archers and, when his armour-bearer refused to kill him, 'Saul took his own sword, and fell upon it' (1 Samuel 31:3-4). (2 Samuel 1:6-10 gives an Amalekite's different claim.)
proTip: Saul's final disobedience ended in his death on Gilboa by his own sword.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: Divine Providence, Guidance and Protection - the Red Sea (Exodus 14:13-14)
question: '...The LORD will fight for you, and you have only to be still.' This statement was made by Moses when the
options: Egyptians were pursuing the Israelites before the Red Sea
Israelites were standing before King Pharaoh
Israelites' chariots were crossing the Red Sea
explanation: Exodus 14:13-14: Moses said this to the terrified Israelites as the Egyptians approached at the Red Sea.
proTip: At the Red Sea: 'The LORD will fight for you'.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: God told Solomon that He would surely tear the kingdom from him and give it to his
explanation: 1 Kings 11:11: 'I will surely tear the kingdom from you and will give it to your servant.' It was fulfilled in Jeroboam.
proTip: Solomon's idolatry cost him the kingdom, given to his servant.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Why did Joab kill Abner?
options: He wanted to avenge the death of his brother
He feared that Abner would take over his post
Abner only came to deceive David
He was an enemy who came to spy on David
explanation: 2 Samuel 3:27, 30: Joab killed Abner 'in revenge for the blood of Asahel his brother.' He also accused Abner of deceiving David (3:25). (The source wrote 'Job'; the name is Joab.)
proTip: Joab killed Abner to avenge his brother Asahel.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: When God told Abraham that Sarah would have a child, Abraham laughed because
options: he already had a child by Hagar
his wife was too old to have a child
he was amused by the promise
explanation: Genesis 17:17: Abraham fell on his face and laughed, saying, 'Shall a child be born to a man who is a hundred years old? Shall Sarah, who is ninety years old, bear a child?'
proTip: Abraham and Sarah laughed because of their old age.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: In the beginning, God created the
explanation: Genesis 1:1: 'In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.'
proTip: Genesis 1:1 is the foundation of belief in God's sovereignty.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: Divine Providence, Guidance and Protection - Moses in Midian (Exodus 2:11-15)
question: Moses fled Egypt to the land of Midian because
options: he was afraid that his crime would be made known
Pharaoh wanted to kill him for the crime he had committed
his countryman asked if he would also kill him
he had killed an Egyptian and buried him in the sand
explanation: Exodus 2:15: 'When Pharaoh heard of it, he sought to kill Moses. But Moses fled from Pharaoh and stayed in the land of Midian.' (Options A and D describe 2:12-14.)
proTip: Pharaoh's attempt to kill Moses made him flee.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: Obedience and Disobedience - Saul and the Amalekites (1 Samuel 15:1-3)
question: The LORD sent Samuel to Saul to go and destroy the Amalekites because
options: they opposed Israel on their way out of Egypt
their land had been given to Israel after the battle

proTip: Israel's stubbornness: refusal to listen to God's word.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets

his assignment would not last long

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets

he had an encounter with Elijah
his inheritance had been taken away

proTip: Ahab sulked because Naboth refused to sell his vineyard.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets

explanation: Isaiah 1:16-17: 'cease to do evil, learn to do good; seek justice, correct oppression; defend the fatherless, plead for the widow.'
proTip: True holiness is shown in justice, not mere ritual.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets

the priests were allowed to worship in the temple

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets

will create a new heart in His people

proTip: Hosea: God wants steadfast love, not mere ritual.

proTip: Naaman's pride was cured when he humbled himself and obeyed.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
question: Daniel became distinguished above all other presidents and satraps because he
options: refused to worship the golden image
had an excellent spirit in him
explanation: Daniel 6:3: 'Then this Daniel became distinguished above all the other presidents and satraps, because an excellent spirit was in him.'
proTip: Daniel 6:3: an excellent spirit.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets

proTip: God used ravens to feed Elijah at Cherith.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: The man appointed by the Holy Spirit to go on the missionary journey with Saul was
explanation: Acts 13:2: 'the Holy Spirit said, "Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them."' Mark came later as their assistant (13:5).
proTip: Barnabas and Saul were set apart by the Holy Spirit.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: The mark of a true disciple according to Jesus Christ is
explanation: John 13:35: 'By this all men will know that you are my disciples, if you have love for one another.'
proTip: Love for one another identifies the disciple.

subject: Christian Religious Studies

proTip: Acts 6:1: neglect of widows in the daily distribution.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: Peter, James and John were asked to keep their experience of the transfiguration secret until
options: the Son of man is raised from the dead
explanation: Matthew 17:9: 'Tell no one the vision, until the Son of man is raised from the dead.'
proTip: The transfiguration was kept secret until after the resurrection.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles

proTip: Vine = Christ; branches = believers.

subject: Christian Religious Studies

question: John declares that for a man to have eternal life he must
options: believe in the Son of God
keep the law of Moses faithfully

proTip: In John, eternal life comes through believing in the Son.

subject: Christian Religious Studies

read from the book of Isaiah
beat everyone that sold and bought
drove out all who sold and bought
explanation: Matthew 21:12: 'And Jesus entered the temple of God and drove out all who sold and bought in the temple.' He did not beat everyone; the scourge was used on the animals (John 2:15).
proTip: Matthew 21:12: Jesus drove out all who sold and bought.

subject: Christian Religious Studies

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles

proTip: The lawyer's question was a test, answered with the parable of the Good Samaritan.

subject: Christian Religious Studies

Jesus rebuked them for lack of faith
the wind and the sea obeyed Jesus
the storm disturbed the boat even with Jesus in it
explanation: Matthew 8:27: 'And the men marveled, saying, "What sort of man is this, that even winds and sea obey him?"'
proTip: They marvelled that the wind and sea obeyed Jesus.

subject: Christian Religious Studies

proTip: Pentecost fulfils Joel 2:28-32.

subject: Christian Religious Studies

did not pray before performing the miracle
did not arrive at the place before the girl died

proTip: The mockery followed 'not dead but sleeping'.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles

requested to be led to Him
explanation: Mark 10:47-48: he cried out, 'Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!' and when rebuked, 'cried out all the more.'
proTip: Bartimaeus' persistent cry for mercy led to his healing.

subject: Christian Religious Studies

declared that He had authority to forgive sin
said sin was the cause of sickness
explanation: Mark 2:5-7: Jesus said to the paralytic, 'Your sins are forgiven.' The scribes thought, 'Why does this man speak thus? It is blasphemy! Who can forgive sins but God alone?'
proTip: Forgiving sins is God's prerogative, hence the charge of blasphemy.

subject: Christian Religious Studies

proTip: Love is the fulfilling of the law.

subject: Christian Religious Studies

proTip: Freedom in Christ is not a licence for evil.

proTip: Baptism = union with Christ's death and resurrection.

subject: Christian Religious Studies

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom

the LORD drove the sea back by a strong east wind
the angel of God stood between them and the Hebrews

subject: Christian Religious Studies

subject: Christian Religious Studies

subject: Christian Religious Studies

desire for more children from God

proTip: Hannah lent Samuel to the LORD and was rewarded with five more children.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom

subject: Christian Religious Studies

it was a turn of affairs brought about by the LORD

proTip: Rehoboam's rejection of the elders also fulfilled God's judgement on Solomon.

proTip: David first entered Saul's court as a musician and armour-bearer.

proTip: The old covenant was written on stone; the new on the heart.

subject: Christian Religious Studies

He said that the LORD was witness to their declaration
explanation: Exodus 24:3-5: Moses wrote down the words, built an altar and 'twelve pillars, according to the twelve tribes of Israel', then sent young men to offer burnt offerings and peace offerings. Both A and B occur in this passage, so check against your key.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom

explanation: Genesis 9:12-13: 'This is the sign of the covenant... I set my bow in the cloud.' Circumcision was the sign of Abraham's covenant.

subject: Christian Religious Studies

question: The signs that God showed to Moses at his call were meant to

enable him to perform miracles before Pharaoh
convince Pharaoh that he was the prophet of God
explanation: Exodus 4:5: 'that they may believe that the LORD, the God of their fathers... has appeared to you.' The signs were first to convince Israel that God had sent Moses. (The scan labelled the fourth option 'E'; I treated it as D.)
proTip: The rod, the leprous hand and the water to blood were credentials for Moses.

subject: Christian Religious Studies

he might pull down Topheth and break Molech into pieces
no one might sacrifice human beings again to Molech
explanation: 2 Kings 23:10: 'he defiled Topheth... that no one might burn his son or his daughter as an offering to Molech.'
proTip: Josiah stopped child sacrifice to Molech.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets

proTip: Ill-gotten wealth from oppression will be lost.

topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets

Avoiding evils and praying for others
Learning to do good and seeking justice

subject: Christian Religious Studies

give them favour in the sight of the nations
give them shepherds after His own heart
explanation: Jeremiah 3:14-15: 'Return, O faithless children... I will give you shepherds after my own heart, who will feed you with knowledge and understanding.'
proTip: Repentance brings restoration and faithful leaders.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets

subject: Christian Religious Studies

proTip: Michael is the guardian prince of Israel in Daniel.

subject: Christian Religious Studies

their mother had played the harlot
explanation: Hosea 2:4-5: 'Upon her children also I will have no pity, because they are children of harlotry. For their mother has played the harlot.'
proTip: Hosea 2:4-5: the children share the mother's guilt as 'children of harlotry'.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
subTopic: Greed and its effects - Ahab's repentance (1 Kings 21:27-29)
