proTip: Even Ahab's humility delayed God's judgement.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
subTopic: Concern for Judah - the fall of Jerusalem (2 Kings 25:7)
question: When the Babylonians captured King Zedekiah, they
options: assaulted his wives in his presence
explanation: 2 Kings 25:7: 'They slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes, and put out the eyes of Zedekiah, and bound him in fetters and took him to Babylon.'
proTip: Zedekiah's last sight was the killing of his sons.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
question: The men who threw Shadrach, Meshach and Abednego into the fire were
options: amazed that the Hebrews were not burnt
assisted to escape from being burnt
explanation: Daniel 3:22: 'the flame of the fire slew those men who took up Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego.' The furnace was heated seven times hotter.
proTip: The furnace killed the soldiers but not the three young men.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
subTopic: Social justice and true religion - Amos 4:1
question: 'Hear this word, you cows of Bashan... who oppress the poor, who crush the needy...' 'Cows of Bashan' in the statement above refers to the
explanation: Amos 4:1: 'Hear this word, you cows of Bashan, who are in the mountain of Samaria.' They urged their husbands, 'Bring, that we may drink!'
proTip: Cows of Bashan = the wealthy, indulgent women of Samaria.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
subTopic: The Supremacy of God - Elijah's flight (1 Kings 19:1-4)
question: 'It is enough; now, O LORD, take away my life; for I am no better than my fathers.' The prayer above was said by Elijah when he
options: had no water to drink at the brook Cherith
learnt that Ahab was looking for him
explanation: 1 Kings 19:1-4: after Jezebel threatened to kill him, Elijah fled, sat under a broom tree and prayed this prayer.
proTip: Elijah's despair followed Jezebel's threat.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
question: In his effort to rebuild the walls of Jerusalem, Nehemiah prayed against the insults of
explanation: Nehemiah 4:1-4: Sanballat and Tobiah mocked the Jews, and Nehemiah prayed, 'Hear, O our God, for we are despised.'
proTip: Sanballat and Tobiah led the opposition to the wall.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: According to Luke, Jesus healed the epileptic boy by
options: telling the boy to have faith
binding the evil spirit in him
explanation: Luke 9:42: 'Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, and healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.'
proTip: Luke: Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Trials and Death of Jesus - Luke 23:46
question: According to Luke, Jesus' last words on the cross were
options: 'Father, into thy hands I commit my spirit'
'Father, forgive them; for they know not what they do'
explanation: Luke 23:46: 'Father, into thy hands I commit my spirit!' And having said this he breathed his last.
proTip: Luke's last words: 'Father, into thy hands I commit my spirit.'

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Parables - the Rich Man and Lazarus (Luke 16:19-31)
question: 'Father Abraham, have mercy upon me, and send Lazarus...' Abraham could not grant the rich man's request because
options: the rich man lived in luxury while on earth
there was a chasm between them
he had no pity on the rich man
his dogs used to lick Lazarus' sores
explanation: Luke 16:26: 'between us and you a great chasm has been fixed, in order that those who would pass from here to you may not be able, and none may cross from there to us.'
proTip: The great chasm made reversal impossible.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: In the story of the transfiguration of Jesus, Moses and Elijah represented the
explanation: Moses stood for the Law and Elijah for the prophets. Their appearing with Jesus showed Him as the fulfilment of both (Matthew 17:3; 5:17).
proTip: Moses = Law; Elijah = Prophets.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Teachings about Himself - the Good Shepherd (John 10:1-9)
question: '...but he who enters by the door is the shepherd of the sheep...' The door in the statement refers to
explanation: John 10:7, 9: 'I am the door of the sheep... if any one enters by me, he will be saved.'
proTip: John 10: Jesus is the door and the Good Shepherd.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: In order to fulfil the law of Moses, Jesus told the leper He had healed to go and
explanation: Luke 5:14: 'go and show yourself to the priest, and make an offering for your cleansing, as Moses commanded.' The question asks for the first step: show himself to the priest (Leviticus 14).
proTip: A healed leper had to be examined by the priest.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: The Jewish religious leaders arrested and imprisoned the apostles the second time because
options: they performed miracles in the name of Jesus
the high priest and the Sadducees accused them of treason
the high priest and the Sadducees were jealous
explanation: Acts 5:17-18: 'the high priest... and all who were with him... were filled with jealousy, they arrested the apostles and put them in the common prison.'
proTip: The second arrest: jealousy over the apostles' success.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: After the mission of the seventy, Jesus declared that He had given
options: authority over all the power of the enemy
the gift of knowledge of the word
explanation: Luke 10:19: 'Behold, I have given you authority to tread upon serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy.'
proTip: The seventy received authority over the enemy's power.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: Jesus did not go immediately to attend to Lazarus who had been reported sick because He
options: wanted His disciples to believe in Him
was too busy attending to His people
did not know how serious the sickness was
explanation: John 11:15: 'for your sake I am glad that I was not there, so that you may believe.' Jesus also said the illness was for the glory of God (11:4).
proTip: The delay was so that the disciples might believe.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Parables - the Wheat and the Tares (Matthew 13:39)
question: In the parable of the wheat and the tares, the harvest time refers to the
explanation: Matthew 13:39: 'the harvest is the close of the age, and the reapers are angels.'
proTip: Harvest = end of the age.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
subTopic: Christian living in the community - 1 Peter 2:17; 3:8
question: Peter teaches that good Christian conduct is characterized by love and
explanation: 1 Peter 2:17: 'Honor all men. Love the brotherhood. Fear God. Honor the emperor.' Love and the fear of God are paired in Peter's household code. (The question is ambiguous, so check against your key.)
proTip: Peter pairs love of the brotherhood with the fear of God.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: Paul teaches that the exercise of spiritual gifts by individual believers should be used to promote
explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:25: the body is arranged 'that there may be no discord in the body, but that the members may have the same care for one another.' Gifts are for mutual cooperation and the common good (12:7). (Check against your key.)
proTip: Gifts promote cooperation, not competition.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
subTopic: Christian living in the community - 1 Peter 5:1-3
question: Peter advises the elders to tend the flock of God with
explanation: 1 Peter 5:2: 'tend the flock of God that is your charge, not by constraint but willingly, not for shameful gain but eagerly.'
proTip: Shepherd the flock willingly and eagerly.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: Paul warned the Thessalonians against the deceit of false teachers concerning
options: activities of the man of sin
explanation: 2 Thessalonians 2:1-3: 'we beg you... not to be quickly shaken in mind... to the effect that the day of the Lord has come. Let no one deceive you.'
proTip: Paul corrected false teaching that the day of the Lord had already come.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: Paul described the gifts he received from the Philippians as
explanation: Philippians 4:18: 'a fragrant offering, a sacrifice acceptable and pleasing to God.'
proTip: The Philippians' gift is 'acceptable and pleasing to God'.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: According to Paul, the purpose of the law is
options: to increase the knowledge of sin
to bring about justification by faith
to promote the faith in the crucified Christ
explanation: Romans 3:20: 'through the law comes knowledge of sin.' Romans 7:7: 'I should not have known sin if it had not been for the law.'
proTip: The law reveals sin; faith in Christ justifies.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: The man who stirred up the people against Paul in Ephesus was
explanation: Acts 19:24-27: Demetrius, a silversmith who made silver shrines of Artemis, called the craftsmen together because Paul's preaching endangered their trade.
proTip: Demetrius the silversmith led the Ephesian riot.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: Paul teaches that believers have been buried and raised with Christ so that they might
options: walk in the newness of life
grow in the knowledge of Christ
explanation: Romans 6:4: 'we were buried therefore with him by baptism into death, so that as Christ was raised from the dead... we too might walk in newness of life.'
proTip: Baptism: buried with Christ, raised to walk in newness of life.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: According to James, because believers hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ, they should
explanation: James 2:1: 'My brethren, show no partiality as you hold the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ.'
proTip: James 2:1: faith in Christ rules out partiality.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: According to Paul's letter to the Philippians, Christ demonstrated His humility by
options: washing the feet of His disciples
taking the form of a servant
explanation: Philippians 2:7: 'he emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being born in the likeness of men.' His death on the cross (2:8) followed. Foot-washing is in John 13.
proTip: Philippians 2:7: He took the form of a servant.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: According to Paul, God would send a strong delusion upon those who will perish because they
options: did not show love to the brethren
explanation: 2 Thessalonians 2:10-11: 'because they refused to love the truth and so be saved. Therefore God sends upon them a strong delusion, to make them believe what is false.'
proTip: Those who refuse the truth are given over to delusion.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: According to Romans, justification is by faith through
options: being filled with the Holy Spirit
explanation: Romans 3:24: 'they are justified by his grace as a gift, through the redemption which is in Christ Jesus.'
proTip: Justified through the redemption in Christ.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: Peter teaches that Christians should prepare for the day of the Lord by
explanation: 2 Peter 3:11-12: 'what sort of persons ought you to be in lives of holiness and godliness, waiting for and hastening the coming of the day of God.'
proTip: 2 Peter 3:11: holy and godly lives.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: David did not allow Abishai to destroy Saul because he
options: believed in the judgement of God
wanted to avoid being guilty before the LORD
wanted to disarm Saul before killing him
wanted to see if Saul would repent eventually
explanation: 1 Samuel 26:9: 'Do not destroy him; for who can put forth his hand against the LORD's anointed, and be guiltless?' David also said God would strike Saul in His own time (26:10), but his stated reason was avoiding guilt.
proTip: David would not harm 'the LORD's anointed'.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: Obedience and Disobedience - rewards of obedience (Proverbs 3:1-2; Deuteronomy 30:15-20)
question: The reward for total obedience to the commandments of God is
explanation: Proverbs 3:1-2: 'let your heart keep my commandments, for length of days and years of life and abundant welfare will they give you.' Deuteronomy 30:19-20 links obedience to life and length of days.
proTip: Obedience to God's commandments brings life and long days.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: The Sovereignty of God - the fall (Genesis 3:20)
question: Adam named his wife Eve because she was
explanation: Genesis 3:20: 'The man called his wife's name Eve, because she was the mother of all living.'
proTip: Eve = the mother of all living.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: What was the immediate reaction of Moses when he cast his rod on the ground at Mount Horeb and it became a serpent?
options: He took it by the tail
explanation: Exodus 4:3: 'he cast it on the ground, and it became a serpent; and Moses ran from it.' God then told him to seize it by the tail.
proTip: Moses first fled, then obeyed God's command to take it by the tail.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: The consequence of King Solomon's failure to keep the LORD's commandment was
options: God's promise to tear away part of the kingdom
the rebellion of the vassal states against his rule
explanation: 1 Kings 11:11-13: God said, 'I will surely tear the kingdom from you,' though He would leave one tribe for David's sake.
proTip: Solomon's idolatry led to the division of the kingdom.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
question: According to Prophet Isaiah, the creative ability of God is likened to that of a
explanation: Isaiah 64:8: 'we are the clay, and thou art our potter; we are all the work of thy hand.' Isaiah 45:9 uses the same imagery.
proTip: Isaiah's image of God as Creator: the potter and the clay.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: 'David departed from there and escaped... and when his brothers and all his father's house heard it...' In the statement above, where did David escape to?
explanation: 1 Samuel 22:1: 'David departed from there and escaped to the cave of Adullam; and when his brothers and all his father's house heard it, they went down there to him.'
proTip: Adullam became David's first refuge and gathering place.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: Decision Making - Solomon and Hiram (1 Kings 5:1)
question: Hiram, King of Tyre, was friendly with King Solomon because he
explanation: 1 Kings 5:1: 'Hiram king of Tyre sent his servants to Solomon, when he heard that they had anointed him king... for Hiram always loved David.'
proTip: Hiram's friendship with David carried over to Solomon.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: 'Go from your country and your kindred and your father's house to the land that I will show you...' Where was Abraham when this command was given?
explanation: Genesis 11:31-12:4: Terah's family settled in Haran, and after Terah died there the LORD said, 'Go from your country...'; Abram left Haran at seventy-five. (Acts 7:2-3 says God first appeared to Abraham in Mesopotamia before Haran, so check against your key.)
proTip: Genesis 12 places the call at Haran; Acts 7 recalls the earlier call in Ur.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
subTopic: Divine Providence, Guidance and Protection - the golden calf (Exodus 32:11-14)
question: The LORD repented of the evil which He intended for His people because Moses
options: burnt the golden calf which the people made
broke the tablets out of his hands
made the people drink of the water of the burnt calf
reminded Him of His promise to Abraham, Isaac and Israel
explanation: Exodus 32:13-14: Moses pleaded, 'Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, thy servants, to whom thou didst swear by thine own self...' And the LORD repented of the evil.
proTip: Moses' intercession based on God's covenant promise saved Israel.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: The altar that Gideon built at the oak of Ophrah was called
explanation: Judges 6:24: 'Then Gideon built an altar there to the LORD, and called it, The LORD is peace.'
proTip: Gideon's altar: Yahweh-shalom, 'The LORD is peace'.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: The second creation story ends with the institution of
explanation: Genesis 2:21-24 ends with the creation of woman and the principle: 'a man leaves his father and his mother and cleaves to his wife, and they become one flesh.' The Sabbath closes the first account (2:1-3).
proTip: Genesis 2 ends with marriage; Genesis 1 ends with the Sabbath.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: The greatest domestic problem King David experienced which almost cost him his kingdom was
options: the proclamation of Adonijah as king
the revolt of Absalom against him
explanation: Absalom's conspiracy forced David to flee from Jerusalem (2 Samuel 15:13-14) and nearly overthrew him.
proTip: Absalom's rebellion was the gravest threat to David's throne.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: The declaration by God that He would make a nation of the son of the slave woman meant that He
options: was not partial towards Isaac and Ishmael
did not like the way Ishmael was sent out by Abraham
was responsible for sending Ishmael out of Abraham's house
explanation: Genesis 21:13: 'I will make a nation of the son of the slave woman also, because he is your offspring.' God recognised Ishmael as Abraham's descendant.
proTip: God keeps His care for Ishmael because he is Abraham's offspring.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: The chief butler said to Pharaoh, 'I remember my faults today...' 'Faults' refer to his
options: sins before he was imprisoned by Pharaoh
inability to identify competent magicians, wise men and interpreters of dreams
forgetting the young Hebrew who interpreted his dream correctly while in prison
explanation: Genesis 41:9-13: the chief butler recalled that Joseph had interpreted his dream accurately in prison, but he had forgotten Joseph for two years (40:23).
proTip: The butler's fault was forgetting Joseph.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: '...The earth produces of itself, first the blade, then the ear, then the full grain in the ear...' The statement above was made by Jesus in the parable of the
explanation: Mark 4:26-29: the kingdom is like a man who scatters seed and the earth produces of itself, first the blade, then the ear. Only Mark records this parable.
proTip: Seed growing secretly = Mark 4:26-29, found only in Mark.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: Peter became frightened as he walked on the sea because
explanation: Matthew 14:30: 'when he saw the wind, he was afraid, and beginning to sink he cried out, "Lord, save me."'
proTip: Peter's fear came from the wind, and his sinking from doubt.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: What did the blind man by the roadside near Jericho do on receiving his sight?
options: He jumped for joy and went away
He thanked Jesus for healing him
He gave praise to God for making him whole
explanation: Luke 18:43: 'immediately he received his sight and followed him, glorifying God.'
proTip: The healed man followed Jesus, glorifying God.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Trials and Death of Jesus - Luke 23:33-39
question: The order of the crucifixion events according to Luke's Gospel is
options: crucifixion, casting lots for His dress, scoffing and mockery
mockery, casting lots for His dress, scoffing and crucifixion
casting lots for His dress, mockery, scoffing and crucifixion
crucifixion, scoffing, mockery and casting lots for His dress
explanation: Luke 23:33-39: they crucified Him (33); divided His garments by casting lots (34); the people stood by and the rulers scoffed (35); the soldiers mocked Him (36).
proTip: Luke's sequence: crucifixion, lots, scoffing, mockery.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Birth and early life of Jesus - Luke 1:13-17
question: The angel told Zechariah that John the Baptist would drink no wine nor strong drink because he would
options: only eat locusts and wild honey
be filled with the Holy Spirit
baptize sinners who would come to him
explanation: Luke 1:15: 'he shall drink no wine nor strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit, even from his mother's womb.'
proTip: John was consecrated from birth and filled with the Spirit.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: What were the two emblems Jesus used during the Last Supper?
options: The bread and the blood of the lamb
The unleavened bread and the fruit of the vine
explanation: At the Last Supper Jesus took bread and the cup, saying 'this is my body' and 'this is my blood of the covenant' (Matthew 26:26-28). The cup contained 'the fruit of the vine' (26:29), commonly called wine. Option C is also defensible, so check against your key.
proTip: The Lord's Supper emblems: the bread and the cup (wine).

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Fellowship in the Early Church - Acts 1:21-22
question: The condition Peter gave for a person that would replace Judas Iscariot was that he must be
options: a disciple of John the Baptist
explanation: Acts 1:21-22: the replacement had to be one who accompanied them from the baptism of John until the ascension, 'a witness to his resurrection.'
proTip: The replacement for Judas had to be a witness to the ministry and the resurrection.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: 'They have no wine.' Jesus' immediate response to the statement above was
options: 'Now draw some out and take it to the steward of the feast'
'O woman, what have you to do with me? My hour has not yet come.'
explanation: John 2:4: 'And Jesus said to her, "O woman, what have you to do with me? My hour has not yet come."' The other statements came later.
proTip: Jesus' first reply to Mary: 'My hour has not yet come'.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: The Macedonians who travelled with Paul to Ephesus were
explanation: Acts 19:29: the crowd 'seized Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians who were Paul's companions in travel.'
proTip: The Macedonians seized at Ephesus: Gaius and Aristarchus.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: 'O faithless and perverse generation, how long am I to be with you and bear with you...' Jesus' statement above was addressed to
options: the Jews because of their unbelief
His disciples because they could not heal
the Pharisees because of their hypocrisy
His own people because they did not give Him honour
explanation: Luke 9:40-41: the boy's father said the disciples could not cast out the spirit; Jesus replied with these words. The rebuke included the disciples and the unbelieving generation.
proTip: The rebuke followed the disciples' failure to heal the boy.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: According to the first Epistle of John, to have the Son is to have
explanation: 1 John 5:12: 'He who has the Son has life; he who has not the Son of God has not life.'
proTip: 1 John 5:12: having the Son means having life.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: In the explanation of the parable of the weeds, Jesus said that the righteous will
options: live forever in the kingdom of God
be set aside from all cause of sin
enter into glory with the Son of man
shine like the sun in their Father's kingdom
explanation: Matthew 13:43: 'Then the righteous will shine like the sun in the kingdom of their Father.'
proTip: The righteous shine like the sun in the Father's kingdom.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Mission to the Gentiles - the Jerusalem Council (Acts 15:28-29)
question: The resolution of the Council at Jerusalem was that the Gentiles should abstain from
options: adultery, greed, strangled meat and divination
homosexuality, idolatry, fornication and strangled meat
idolatry, unchastity, strangled meat and blood
explanation: Acts 15:29: 'abstain from what has been sacrificed to idols and from blood and from what is strangled and from unchastity.'
proTip: Council's four requirements: idols, blood, strangled meat, unchastity.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: '...And I will say to my soul, "Soul, you have ample goods laid up for many years; take your ease, eat, drink, be merry."' God's response to the statement above was that
options: the servant should enter into the rest of his Lord
his soul was required of him
his soul should be satisfied with his increase
he should lay up more treasures for himself
explanation: Luke 12:20: 'But God said to him, "Fool! This night your soul is required of you; and the things you have prepared, whose will they be?"'
proTip: The rich fool lost his life and his goods the same night.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Trials and Death of Jesus - Peter's denial (Luke 22:54-57)
question: Before the cock crowed, Peter denied Jesus three times. Who was the first person to recognise him as one of the disciples?
explanation: Luke 22:56-57: 'a maid, seeing him as he sat in the light and gazing at him, said, "This man also was with him." But he denied it.'
proTip: Peter's first challenger was a maid in the high priest's courtyard.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
subTopic: Miracles - the woman with the flow of blood (Mark 5:25-34)
question: The woman with the flow of blood touched the garment of Jesus because
options: she had heard the reports about Jesus
she had suffered much under many physicians
the crowd could not allow her to speak to Jesus
she believed that she would be well
explanation: Mark 5:28: 'For she said, "If I touch even his garments, I shall be made well."' Jesus said, 'Your faith has made you well.'
proTip: Her touch expressed faith in Jesus' power.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: In Paul's letter to the Thessalonians, believers were admonished to prepare for the Second Coming of Christ by
explanation: 1 Thessalonians 5:6: 'let us not sleep, as others do, but let us keep awake and be sober.'
proTip: Prepare for the Lord's day: stay awake and sober.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: Paul taught the Romans that while they were yet enemies of God, they were reconciled to Him by the
explanation: Romans 5:10: 'while we were enemies we were reconciled to God by the death of his Son.'
proTip: Reconciliation comes through Christ's death.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: Paul declared to the believers in Corinth that no one can say 'Jesus is Lord' except by
explanation: 1 Corinthians 12:3: 'no one can say "Jesus is Lord" except by the Holy Spirit.'
proTip: The confession 'Jesus is Lord' is a work of the Holy Spirit.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
subTopic: Christian living in the community - 1 Peter 1:6-7
question: According to Peter, the genuineness of Christian faith is tested by
explanation: 1 Peter 1:7: 'so that the genuineness of your faith, more precious than gold which though perishable is tested by fire, may be found to result in praise and glory and honor.'
proTip: Faith is tested by fire, as gold is refined.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: In Colossians, Paul admonished believers not to lie to one another because they
options: were joint heirs with Christ in the kingdom
were waiting for the Second Coming of Christ
had put off the old nature with its practices
had known the truth from the very beginning
explanation: Colossians 3:9-10: 'Do not lie to one another, seeing that you have put off the old nature with its practices and have put on the new nature.'
proTip: Believers must live out the new nature they have put on.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: Paul teaches that believers who maintain good conduct before governing authorities shall
explanation: Romans 13:3: 'Would you have no fear of him who is in authority? Then do what is good, and you will receive his approval.'
proTip: Good conduct earns the approval of authorities.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
subTopic: Christian living in the community - 1 Peter 5:4
question: According to Peter, when the chief Shepherd would be manifested, the elders would obtain the
explanation: 1 Peter 5:4: 'when the chief Shepherd is manifested you will obtain the unfading crown of glory.'
proTip: Faithful elders receive the unfading crown of glory.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: Paul boasted about the believers in Corinth for their
explanation: 2 Corinthians 9:2: 'I know your readiness, of which I boast about you to the people of Macedonia, saying that Achaia has been ready since last year.' The context is the collection for the saints (9:1).
proTip: Paul boasted of Corinth's readiness to give for the saints.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: God exalted the name of Jesus above every other name in heaven and on earth because
options: Jesus was born in the likeness of man
as Son of God, He counted equality with God a thing to be grasped
in humility, He counted others better than Himself
He humbled Himself to be born in human form and was obedient to death
explanation: Philippians 2:8-9: 'he humbled himself and became obedient unto death, even death on a cross. Therefore God has highly exalted him.'
proTip: Exaltation followed humiliation and obedience to death.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
subTopic: Obedience and Disobedience - Joshua and Ai (Joshua 7:6)
question: How did Joshua react to the defeat of the Israelites by the men of Ai?
explanation: Joshua 7:6: 'Then Joshua rent his clothes, and fell to the earth upon his face before the ark of the LORD until the evening.' He also prayed (7:7-9), but tearing his clothes was his first reaction.
proTip: Joshua's immediate reaction was tearing his clothes and falling on his face.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
subTopic: Social justice, true religion and divine love - Hosea 14:9
question: Hosea declares that the upright walk in the ways of the LORD, but transgressors
explanation: Hosea 14:9: 'the ways of the LORD are right, and the upright walk in them, but transgressors stumble in them.'
proTip: Hosea 14:9: transgressors stumble in God's ways.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
subTopic: Concern for Judah - the exile (2 Kings 25:11-12)
question: After Nebuchadnezzar had destroyed Jerusalem, he took the inhabitants into exile but left behind the
explanation: 2 Kings 25:12: 'the captain of the guard left some of the poorest of the land to be vinedressers and plowmen.'
proTip: Babylon left behind only the poorest to work the land.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
question: According to Amos, the type of famine God said He would send upon the people of Israel was
options: not hearing the word of the LORD
hunger for baskets of summer fruits
explanation: Amos 8:11: 'I will send a famine on the land; not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the LORD.'
proTip: The famine Amos announced was spiritual: no word from God.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
question: '...The soul that sins shall die.' The statement above by Prophet Ezekiel means that
options: a sinner shall not escape punishment
the wages of sin is death
God will judge the soul of a sinner
every person is responsible for his own sin
explanation: Ezekiel 18:20: 'The soul that sins shall die. The son shall not suffer for the iniquity of the father... the righteousness of the righteous shall be upon himself.' It teaches individual responsibility.
proTip: Ezekiel 18: individual responsibility for sin.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
subTopic: Greed and its effects - Hiel of Bethel (1 Kings 16:34)
question: The consequence of Hiel's building of Jericho was that he
options: was made a commander in Ahab's army
was highly respected by his tribe
explanation: 1 Kings 16:34: 'Hiel of Bethel built Jericho; he laid its foundations at the cost of Abiram his first-born, and set up its gates at the cost of his youngest son Segub, according to the word of the LORD' spoken by Joshua (Joshua 6:26).
proTip: Joshua's curse on the rebuilder of Jericho was fulfilled in Hiel's two sons.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
question: '...I send you to the people of Israel, to a nation of rebels...' The statement above was God's message to
explanation: Ezekiel 2:3: 'Son of man, I send you to the people of Israel, to a nation of rebels, who have rebelled against me.'
proTip: 'Son of man' and 'nation of rebels' mark Ezekiel's call.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
question: Daniel was set up to be thrown to the lions by the
explanation: Daniel 6:4-5: the presidents and satraps sought a ground of complaint against Daniel, and plotted against him because of his devotion to God.
proTip: Daniel's enemies were the jealous presidents and satraps.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
question: According to Hosea, one of the punishments for the sins of Israel was that
options: they would not receive divine revelation
they would eat but would not be satisfied
the LORD would send famine upon the land
explanation: Hosea 4:10: 'They shall eat, but not be satisfied; they shall play the harlot, but not multiply.'
proTip: Hosea 4:10: eat but not be satisfied.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
subTopic: Greed and its effects - Gehazi (2 Kings 5:25-27)
question: Elisha knew of the covetous act of Gehazi because
options: he went with him in spirit
he saw the gifts with him
explanation: 2 Kings 5:26: 'Did not my heart go with you when the man turned from his chariot to meet you?' (The scan says 'Elijah'; the prophet is Elisha.)
proTip: Elisha's spiritual insight exposed Gehazi's greed.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Moses sent men to spy out the land of Canaan in order to
options: know if it was god or bad
know if it was flowing with milk and honey
explanation: According to the narrative in Numbers 13:17-20, Moses sent the spies into the land of Canaan to see what the land was, whether it was good or bad, and whether the people who dwelt in it were strong or weak, few or many.
proTip: Pay close attention to the specific tactical motives described in pentateuchal narratives regarding the spy missions into Canaan.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: The two sons of Samuel that became Judges in Israel were
explanation: According to 1 Samuel 8:1-2, when Samuel grew old, he made his sons judges over Israel; the name of his firstborn was Joel, and the name of his second, Abijah, and they judged in Beersheba.
proTip: Distinguish Samuel's sons (Joel and Abijah) from Eli's corrupt sons (Hophni and Phinehas).

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Let us make man in our image, after our likeness..." In the statement above, 'in our image' implies man
options: being a representative of God and fellow men
becoming the exact picture of God
explanation: In Genesis 1:26-27, being created in the image and likeness of God speaks of humanity's unique spiritual, moral, and rational reflection of God's attributes, establishing a distinct status of resemblance and relationship with the Creator.
proTip: The imago Dei emphasizes human likeness to God in character, dominion, and spiritual capacity, distinct from physical form.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: The murmuring of the congregation in the wilderness against Moses and Aaron were an indication of the people's
options: fear of dying by the sword
inability to get to the promise land
explanation: Throughout the Exodus journey, constant murmuring against Moses and Aaron reflected the Israelites' underlying lack of faith in God's protective provision and divine guidance.
proTip: Relate wilderness murmuring directly to a failure of faith in Yahweh's sustaining power.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: When the glory of the LORD appeared to Moses and Aaron in the wilderness of Zin, the Lord said they should
options: tell the rock before their eyes to yield its water
strike the rock with rod to bring out water for them
fetch water for the people and their cattle
tell the people to go around the rock
explanation: According to Numbers 20:7-8, God explicitly instructed Moses to take the rod and assemble the congregation, and speak to the rock before their eyes to yield water, rather than striking it.
proTip: Note the exact shift in instruction between Exodus 17 (strike the rock) and Numbers 20 (speak to the rock).

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: The last event that boosted Gideon's courage to go against the Midianites was the
options: appearance of the angel who called him a man of valour
sign in which God caused the dew to be on the fleece
test God gave Gideon's men at the waterside
dream told by the Midianites about the barley bread
explanation: As recorded in Judges 7:13-15, Gideon overheard a Midianite soldier recounting a dream about a cake of barley bread tumbling into the camp of Midian and overturning it, which gave Gideon the final surge of courage to attack.
proTip: Track the progressive signs given to Gideon: the fleece, the reduction of troops, and finally the overheard enemy dream.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: At the confirmation of the covenant, after Moses had addressed the people, they answered and said,
options: We are going to obey the Lord our God
to beware of false prophets and teachers
All that the Lord has spoken we will do
explanation: In Exodus 24:3, after Moses recounted all the words of the Lord and the ordinances, all the people answered with one voice and said, "All the words which the Lord has spoken we will do."
proTip: Memorize standard covenant response formulas in Exodus ('All that the Lord has spoken we will do').

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Saul visited the witch of Endor when he was besieged by the
explanation: According to 1 Samuel 28:4-7, King Saul was deeply afraid when the Philistine army encamped at Shunem, leading him to consult the medium at Endor.
proTip: Connect Saul's spiritual desperation at Endor directly with the impending Philistine battle at Gilboa.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Why did Saul tell the Kenites to go away from among the Amalekites?
options: God did not tell him to destroy the Kenites
The Kenites showed kindness to Israel
The Kenites had blood covenant with Israel
explanation: As noted in 1 Samuel 15:6, Saul warned the Kenites to depart from the Amalekites because they had shown kindness to all the people of Israel when they came up out of Egypt.
proTip: Remember historical alliances maintained during Israel's conquest and judicial punishments.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: ..And they shall be my people, and I will be their God..." This covenant was made with Israel through prophet
explanation: This specific formula regarding the new covenant where God writes His law on their hearts and states "I will be their God, and they shall be my people" is famously prophesied by Jeremiah in Jeremiah 31:33.
proTip: Associate the New Covenant prophecy ('law written on hearts') explicitly with Jeremiah.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: How many sons of Jesse passed before Samuel before David was chosen as King?
explanation: According to 1 Samuel 16:10, Jesse made seven of his sons pass before Samuel, and Samuel said to Jesse, "The Lord has not chosen these" before asking if there were any other youths.
proTip: Count carefully: Jesse presented seven sons before Samuel before David was fetched from the sheepfolds (making eight total sons).

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Whoever does not come out after Saul and Samuel, so shall it be done to his oxen!" What came upon the people as a result of this declaration?
options: The power of the Lord came upon them
The dread of the Lord fell upon them
The spirit of the Lord came upon them
The word of the Lord came to them
explanation: According to 1 Samuel 11:7, after Saul cut the yoke of oxen in pieces and sent them throughout Israel with this threat, the dread of the Lord fell upon the people, and they came out as one man.
proTip: Note the psychological and spiritual impact of leadership ultimatums in early Israelite monarchy accounts.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: ..Do not forsake her, and she will keep you, love her and she will guard you..." refers to
explanation: In Proverbs 4:6, wisdom is personified, and the reader is admonished: "Do not forsake her, and she will keep you; love her, and she will guard you."
proTip: Recognize personified wisdom literature motifs in the Book of Proverbs.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Joseph was made prime minister in Egypt because he
options: interpreted the dreams of Pharaoh's servants in the prison
resisted the temptation by Potiphar's wife
was a faithful and upright man
interpreted Pharaoh's dream and counselled him what to do
explanation: As recorded in Genesis 41:39-41, Pharaoh elevated Joseph to governor over all Egypt directly because Joseph successfully interpreted Pharaoh's troubling dreams and provided a wise administrative plan to handle the coming famine.
proTip: Differentiate Joseph's imprisonment interpretation from his ultimate elevation, which was driven by interpreting Pharaoh's royal dreams.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Nehemiah in exile functioned as the King's
explanation: According to Nehemiah 1:11, Nehemiah held the high and trusted position of cupbearer to King Artaxerxes of Persia.
proTip: Nehemiah's role as royal cupbearer provided him both high access to the king and resources for rebuilding Jerusalem.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
question: In days of Uzziah, Isaiah saw a vision concerning
explanation: Isaiah 1:1 explicitly states: "The vision of Isaiah the son of Amoz, which he saw concerning Judah and Jerusalem in the days of Uzziah, Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah."
proTip: Always verify prophetic book superscriptions for precise regional scopes (e.g., Judah and Jerusalem for Isaiah).

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
question: God said that any member of Ahab's family who died in the open country would be
explanation: According to 1 Kings 21:24 (and 1 Kings 14:11), the prophetic judgment against the house of Ahab specified that anyone belonging to Ahab who died in the city would be eaten by dogs, and any who died in the open country would be eaten by the birds of the air.
proTip: Distinguish the fate of city-dwellers (eaten by dogs) from open-country casualties (eaten by birds) in Ahab's curse.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
subTopic: Social justice/True religion and Divine love
question: Take away all iniquity; accept that which is good..." What was the iniquity Hosea was referring to in the statement above?
explanation: In Hosea 14:2-3, the prophet calls Israel to repent of her spiritual unfaithfulness and idolatry, explicitly mentioning that they will no longer say 'Our god' to the work of their hands, pointing directly to idolatry.
proTip: Hosea's central theme of spiritual adultery is synonymous with covenant unfaithfulness through idolatry.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
question: According to Jeremiah, the role of the shepherds which God will give to His people is to
options: feed the people with knowledge and understanding
heal the guilt of the people
gather the scattered children of Israel
explanation: According to Jeremiah 3:15, God promises to give His people shepherds after His own heart who will feed them with knowledge and understanding.
proTip: Memorize Jeremiah 3:15 as the standard prophetic standard for spiritual leadership in Judah.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
question: King Nebuchadnezzar assembled the satraps, the prefects and the governors to
explanation: According to Daniel 3:2-3, King Nebuchadnezzar assembled all the satraps, prefects, governors, and officials for the dedication of the golden image he had set up in the plain of Dura.
proTip: Distinguish Daniel 2 (dream interpretation assembly) from Daniel 3 (golden image dedication assembly).

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION A: Themes from Creation to the Division of the Kingdom
question: Where did Elijah kill all the prophets of Baal after the contest with Ahab?
explanation: According to 1 Kings 18:40, after the contest on Mount Carmel, Elijah brought the prophets of Baal down to the brook Kishon and killed them there.
proTip: Note the geographic distinction: the contest took place *on* Carmel, but the execution of the prophets occurred down at the brook Kishon.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
question: ..The fathers have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge..."
options: parents are punished for the sins of their children
children are punished for the sins of their parents
parents are punished for the sins of their grandparents
great grandchildren are punished for the sins of their forefathers
explanation: This popular proverb addressed in Ezekiel 18 and Jeremiah 31 expressed the popular fatalistic view among the exiles that children were suffering and being punished for the sins and wickedness committed by their parents and ancestors.
proTip: Understand that the sour grapes proverb encapsulates generational punishment beliefs refuted by Ezekiel's doctrine of individual responsibility.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
question: After Jonah had been thrown into the sea and the sea ceased from its raging, the men with him
options: praised the Lord for saving them
feared the LORD, offered sacrifice and made vows
rowed hard to bring the ship back to land
explanation: According to Jonah 1:16, when the sea ceased its raging after Jonah was cast overboard, the men feared the Lord exceedingly, and they offered a sacrifice to the Lord and made vows.
proTip: Note the profound spiritual impact Jonah's voyage had on the pagan sailors, leading them to worship Yahweh.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION B: Themes from the Division of the Kingdom to the Return from Exile and the Prophets
question: Zedekiah, the king of Judah, was captured by the army of the Chaldeans
explanation: According to 2 Kings 25:4-5 and Jeremiah 39:5, the army of the Chaldeans pursued King Zedekiah and overtook him in the plains of Jericho, after which he was brought up to the king of Babylon at Riblah.
proTip: Differentiate the capture location (plains of Jericho) from the subsequent trial/judgment location (Riblah).

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: Two Christian virtues to be learned in the story of the good Samaritan are
explanation: In the parable of the Good Samaritan (Luke 10:33-37), the Samaritan is moved by deep compassion and acts with mercy toward the wounded traveler, exemplifying active neighborly love.
proTip: Compassion and mercy are core ethical takeaways highlighted in Luke's Good Samaritan account.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: What have you to do with us, O Son of God? Have you come here to torment us before the time?" This statement reveals that the demoniacs in the country of the Gadarenes
options: recognised the supreme power of Jesus
were threatened by the power of Jesus
did not expect Jesus to come to them at that time
explanation: As recorded in Matthew 8:29 (and parallel accounts), the demonic forces instantly recognized Jesus' divine identity ("Son of God") and His absolute authority to judge and torment them.
proTip: Demonic pronouncements in the Gospels consistently reflect supernatural recognition of Jesus' divine sovereignty.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: According to Luke, the mandate given to the twelve at their commissioning was to
options: rid the entire region of Galilee of evil spirits
preach the gospel to the poor
preach the kingdom of God and heal
go about doing good to all people
explanation: According to Luke 9:1-2, Jesus called the twelve together and gave them power and authority over all demons, and to cure diseases, and sent them out to preach the kingdom of God and to heal.
proTip: Match the synoptic mission mandate for the Twelve: preaching the kingdom of God and healing the sick.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: According to John, the accusation of the Jews levelled against Jesus before Pilate was that He was
explanation: According to John 18:30, when Pilate asked what accusation they brought against Jesus, the Jews answered, "If this man were not an evildoer (or malefactor), we would not have handed him over."
proTip: Pay close attention to Gospel-specific phrasing during the Roman trials before Pilate.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: Go and learn what this means, 'I desire mercy and not sacrifice'...
explanation: According to Matthew 9:9-13, when the Pharisees questioned Jesus for eating with tax collectors and sinners, Jesus quoted Hosea 6:6, telling them to go and learn what 'I desire mercy and not sacrifice' means.
proTip: Connect Jesus' quotation of 'mercy not sacrifice' directly to table fellowship with tax collectors and sinners.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: Jesus did not go with the centurion to heal his servant because he
options: spoke to Jesus as a man under authority
was not worthy for Jesus to come under his roof
explanation: In the account of the Centurion at Capernaum (Matthew 8:8 / Luke 7:6), the centurion sent friends to say, "Lord, do not trouble yourself, for I am not worthy to have you come under my roof," demonstrating profound humility and faith in the power of Jesus' word alone.
proTip: The centurion's reasoning for declining Jesus' physical visit was his profound sense of unworthiness combined with absolute faith in Jesus' spoken word.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: The disciples celebrated the Passover with Jesus because
options: He was going to be betrayed by one of them
it was the first day of unleavened bread
they had sacrificed the passover lamb
they wanted to keep the Passover feast with Him
explanation: According to Matthew 26:17 (and parallel synoptic accounts), on the first day of Unleavened Bread, the disciples came to Jesus asking where He wanted them to prepare for Him to eat the Passover.
proTip: Sync the Last Supper preparation timeline with the opening day of the Feast of Unleavened Bread.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: According to Matthew, true wisdom is
options: seeking first God's kingdom and His righteousness
knowing the truth and doing it at all times
to beware of false prophets and teachers
explanation: In the Sermon on the Mount (Matthew 6:33), Jesus establishes the pursuit of God's kingdom and His righteousness as the ultimate priority of true wisdom, ensuring all earthly needs are secondary.
proTip: Matthew 6:33 ('Seek ye first the kingdom of God') is the hallmark verse for Christian priority and wisdom.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: The condition Jesus required from Jairus in order to heal his daughter was that he should
options: put out those weeping in the house
explanation: According to Mark 5:36 (and Luke 8:50), when word came that the synagogue official's daughter was dead, Jesus immediately said to Jairus, "Do not fear, only believe."
proTip: Faith overcoming fear is the primary condition Jesus demands in Jairus' raising narrative.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: According to Peter's speech on the day of Pentecost, God made Jesus
explanation: In Acts 2:36, concluding his Pentecost sermon, Peter declares with absolute assurance: "Let all the house of Israel therefore know assuredly that God has made him both Lord and Christ, this Jesus whom you crucified."
proTip: Acts 2:36 is Peter's core proclamation establishing Jesus' dual divine titles of Lord and Christ.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved." The men who taught the above came from
explanation: According to Acts 15:1, certain men came down from Judea (Jerusalem) to Antioch and were teaching the brethren, "Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved."
proTip: Trace the Judaizers who triggered the Jerusalem Council back to their origin in Jerusalem/Judea.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: According to John, Jesus said the work of God is
options: feeding the hungry who are in need
believing in Him whom He had sent
explanation: According to John 6:28-29, when the crowd asked what they must do to be doing the works of God, Jesus answered, "This is the work of God, that you believe in him whom he has sent."
proTip: John 6:29 uniquely defines the fundamental 'work of God' as faith in Jesus Christ.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: What shall we do to these men? For that a notable sign has been performed through them is manifested to all..."
options: The high priest tore his garments
explanation: According to Acts 4:15-16, after Peter and John healed the lame man at the Beautiful Gate, the Sanhedrin conferred among themselves, admitting that a notable sign had been performed which they could not deny.
proTip: Note the reaction of the religious authorities when confronted with undeniable apostolic miracles in early Acts.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: Why was Paul arrested and detained at Philippi?
options: He never stopped proclaiming Jesus as Lord and Saviour
The Jews did not want him to preach in the Gentiles' territories
He cast out the spirit of soothsaying from a slave girl
He was preaching the unknown God
explanation: According to Acts 16:16-24, Paul and Silas were arrested and beaten in Philippi after Paul cast the spirit of divination out of a slave girl, destroying her masters' source of lucrative fortune-telling income.
proTip: Economic disruption caused by exorcism was the direct trigger for Paul's imprisonment in Philippi.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: Jesus said His disciples had been made clean by
options: the word He spoke to them
explanation: According to John 15:3, during the Farewell Discourse, Jesus told His disciples, "Already you are clean because of the word that I have spoken to you."
proTip: Connect spiritual cleansing in John 15 directly to the transformative power of Jesus' word.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION C: Themes from the four Gospels and Acts of the Apostles
question: Following the death of Stephen, the only group of believers not scattered by the great persecution against the Jerusalem Church were the
explanation: According to Acts 8:1, following the martyrdom of Stephen and the ensuing severe persecution, all the believers were scattered throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles who remained in Jerusalem.
proTip: Note the strategic resilience of the Apostles staying behind in Jerusalem during the post-Stephen dispersion.

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: The first set in the order of hierarchy of spiritual gifts enumerated by Paul are
explanation: According to 1 Corinthians 12:28, Paul outlines the hierarchical arrangement of functions in the church: "And God has appointed in the church first apostles, second prophets, third teachers..."
proTip: Memorize Paul's order of foundational church offices in 1 Corinthians 12:28 (Apostles, Prophets, Teachers).

subject: Christian Religious Studies
topic: SECTION D: Themes from Selected Epistles
question: According to Galatians, Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by

subject: Christian Religious Studies

executes God's wrath on the wrongdoer
rules as influenced by the people

proTip: Romans 13 establishes civil government as God's instrument for executing wrath upon evildoers.

subject: Christian Religious Studies

love and God rests upon them

subject: Christian Religious Studies

subject: Christian Religious Studies

release from prison by the Jews
healing of the lame man at the Beautiful Gate
address to the disciples about replacing Judas

triumphal entry and cleansing of the temple

question: Jesus said, 'Take heart, it is I; have no fear,' when He was
options: appearing to two disciples on the road to Emmaus
walking on the sea at night
appearing to Mary Magdalene at the tomb

did His work on the Sabbath
was unhappy that He had healed the man
called God His Father, making Himself equal with God
